final_answer: the sky appears blue during the day due to Rayleigh scattering, where shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scatter more in the atmosphere than longer wavelengths (red/orange). although violet has the shortest wavelength, our eyes are more sensitive to blue, and some violet is absorbed by the upper atmosphere. at sunset, sunlight travels a longer path through the atmosphere, scattering most of the blue light out of the direct beam. this leaves longer wavelengths (reds/oranges) to dominate the light reaching our eyes, creating the reddish hue. Rayleigh scattering’s inverse fourth-power dependence on wavelength (1/λ⁴) explains why blue scatters more during the day but is largely filtered out at sunset.
